CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the already-announced matching response on the $16B List 2 (effective 23 August) and the contingent $60B package if Washington proceeds with List 3, but do not add fresh tariffs or non-tariff measures this week. Reopen talks without new purchase or structural commitments until the United States freezes the proposed $200B List 3 (now being considered at 25%). Hold the yuan in an orderly range; do not weaponize depreciation.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. Live 25% tariffs on ~$34B (6 July) plus imminent List 2, a Section 301 design aimed at Made in China 2025 sectors, and USTR’s 1 August signal that List 3 (~$200B, ~6,000 lines) may rise from 10% to 25% put a large slice of US-bound exports at risk (timeline 2018-07-06, 2018-07-10, 2018-08-01). The April ZTE denial order showed Washington can idle a national champion via component controls; the 13 July lift after a $1.4B penalty, board purge and 10-year monitors removed the immediate shutdown but left a suspended ban hanging. FX is the other pressure point: CNY weakened from ~6.34 to 6.933 per dollar by 15 August (~9.4%), Trump has already accused Beijing of manipulation, and a disorderly break toward 7 would risk 2015-style outflows even though reserves remain ~$3.13T. That said, the real economy is not breaking: industrial production is still ~6.1% y/y, merchandise exports remain around $205B (SA), and the discount rate is unchanged at 2.9%. China has already used most of its dollar-for-dollar tariff room (Politico 3–5 August: a $60B list would cover nearly all ~$130B of US goods China buys). The 19 May joint statement — China to “significantly increase” purchases, Mnuchin calling the war “on hold” — collapsed ten days later when the White House proceeded with $50B tariffs, so unilateral concede_purchases would buy nothing and look weak. Further unforced escalation now would also make List 3 at 25% more likely and exhaust remaining leverage. The disciplined stance is therefore hold the announced retaliation, keep the door open to talks with no new commitments, and wait out the List 3 comment period (closes 5 September).
key_factors: List 1 live ($34B) and List 2 ($16B) set for 23 August; List 3 (~$200B) still proposed but rate may rise to 25%
China cannot match US tariff coverage dollar-for-dollar; $60B contingent list nearly exhausts US goods imports
CNY down ~9.4% since February; depreciation offsets some tariffs but risks capital flight and a currency-war charge
Real economy still expanding (IP ~6.1% y/y, exports holding); threat is prospective more than realized
May 19 purchase-truce collapsed on May 29 — do not concede unilaterally again
ZTE shutdown risk demonstrated then settled; export-control vulnerability remains

sources_cited.excerpt: List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods. China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation the same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 product lines).
At Trump's direction, USTR says it is considering raising the proposed List 3 rate from 10% to 25%.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
China industrial production still 106.1 (same period previous year = 100) as of 2018-08-01.
China merchandise exports SA still $205.0B in August 2018 window vs $191.3B in March; not a collapse.
China reserves ex-gold ~$3.13T as of 2018-08-01, down only ~1% over the window.
China threatened 3 August to tax an additional $60B of US goods (up to 25%, 5,207 categories) if the US proceeds with new levies on Chinese goods.
If carried through, China would be imposing tariffs on nearly all ~$130B of US goods it imports and cannot match US coverage dollar-for-dollar.
China announced additional 25% tariffs on $16B of US goods starting 23 August, matching the US List 2 formalization.
Commerce lifted the ZTE denial order 13 July after $1B penalty, $400M escrow, leadership overhaul and 10-year monitors.
